query: Why do some Amazon products receive predominantly negative reviews, and which factors contribute the most?

per_column.name: performance_gap_type
per_column.rationale: A typed taxonomy of concrete product-failure modes is a genuine grouping axis for the 'which factors' part of the query. However it is dominated by 'not_present' (196 of ~250), reflecting that most rows here are media reviews with no hardware spec gap; this near-constancy weakens its leverage. Values seen are defensible: media/subjective reviews correctly mark 'not_present', so no invented specifics observed.

per_column.name: product_category
per_column.rationale: Product category is a strong, well-distributed axis to compare why negativity clusters (books vs music vs electronics). Sample categorisations (toy doll -> toy_game, Lamott book -> media_book, Eamon -> media_music, Bicycle Thieves -> media_film) are sound readings of the text. The skincare cream mapped to 'other' is a mild imprecision but not a hallucination.

per_column.name: reviewer_expectation_mismatch
per_column.rationale: Directly targets the 'why negative' question by typing the nature of unmet expectation (genre, sequel comparison, price/value, brand). Distinct from category and gap_type, so adds a real axis. Grounding is mostly sound: Lamott review flagged 'genre_expectation' is warranted (reader expected faith/kid writing, got politics). Some 'not_present' assignments are conservative and acceptable; risk of subjective over-labeling exists but samples do not show contradiction.

per_column.name: complaint_specificity
per_column.rationale: An ordinal specificity score (1-3) could help weight or rank complaints, giving some modeling leverage. But it is a coarse, thinly-defined scale with heavy NULLs (115) and no rubric, limiting interpretability. Grounding is uncertain: sample rows are all scored '2.0' regardless of quite different content, suggesting the value may not be reliably derived from row-specific evidence, though nothing is outright contradicted.

judge.rationale: Collectively the columns give several genuine, mostly independent axes (category, expectation-mismatch type, failure-mode type) that materially support diagnosing why products are reviewed negatively. product_category and reviewer_expectation_mismatch are the strongest; performance_gap_type is useful but near-constant on this media-heavy sample; complaint_specificity is the weakest, being a vaguely defined scale with heavy NULLs and uniform sample values. Values in the evidence samples are reasonable readings of the source text with no observed hallucinated specifics; conservative 'not_present'/NULL on silent rows is appropriate.
